content.text:
Here's what I found before touching anything. Your global Claude Code is heavily customized in three places:

- **`~/.claude/settings.json`** — routes all traffic through a third-party proxy (`agentrouter.org`) with a hardcoded token, forces every model tier to `claude-opus-5`, and registers three gstack hooks.
- **`~/.zshrc` (lines 16–26)** — exports the same proxy URL/token and model overrides into your shell, so they apply even if the settings file is cleaned.
- **`~/.claude/`** — 270 agents, 56 skills, the official plugin marketplace, plus session/project history. You're also logged into a real Anthropic account (`emutembei@appliedhealthanalytics.org`).

"Original configuration" could mean a few different depths here, and some of them are irreversible, so let me confirm scope before I do anything.

Now the picture is clear: Claude Code is routed through the agentrouter.org proxy via both the settings and shell config, with custom hooks, 270 agents, 56 skills, and the official plugin marketplace all installed globally—plus a real logged-in Anthropic OAuth account. I'm considering resetting to the original config.

The scope of "reset" is ambiguous though — do they want to keep gstack's skills/agents, or wipe everything back to a fresh install? I should ask two things: what scope of reset they want (settings only, settings + hooks + agents/skills, or a full wipe including history and login), and whether to also revert the zshrc exports, which I'd recommend removing since they'd override any settings changes anyway.

questions.prompt: How deep should the reset go?

options.label: Config only (Recommended) — reset settings.json to stock, remove the agentrouter proxy/model overrides and gstack hooks. Keep your 270 agents, 56 skills, plugins, and history.
Config + extensions — everything above, plus remove the global agents/, skills/, and plugins/ directories (wipes gstack).
Full factory reset — delete ~/.claude and ~/.claude.json entirely. Wipes config, agents, skills, plugins, all session/project history, and logs you out.

questions.prompt: Your ~/.zshrc also exports ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL/AUTH_TOKEN and model overrides. These override any settings file, so a reset is incomplete without addressing them.

options.label: Remove those lines from ~/.zshrc (Recommended) — required for a true reset to official Anthropic endpoints.
Comment them out instead, so you can re-enable the proxy later.
Leave ~/.zshrc untouched — I'll handle it myself.
Yes (Recommended) — snapshot ~/.claude, ~/.claude.json, and ~/.zshrc to a timestamped folder first.

Claude Code is now reset to a clean, stock global configuration. The CLI itself (v2.1.250, native install at `~/.local/bin/claude`) is untouched — only its configuration and state were removed.

**What was deleted:**

| Item | Contents removed |
|---|---|
| `~/.claude/` | settings.json, 270 agents, 56 skills, plugin marketplace, projects/sessions/history, backups |
| `~/.claude.json` | global state, onboarding flags, MCP servers, 4 project entries, account record |
| `~/.zshrc` lines 15–27 | AgentRouter proxy block (token, base URL, model overrides) |
| Keychain `Claude Code-credentials` | OAuth token — you are now signed out |

**Verification:** a shell started with a fully isolated environment shows no `ANTHROPIC_*` or `CLAUDE_CODE_*` variables, and `~/.zshenv`, `~/.zprofile`, `/etc/zshrc`, `/etc/zprofile`, and `launchctl` are all clean. Next launch will hit Anthropic's official API endpoints with default model selection.

One caveat on my earlier check: my first "fresh shell" test still showed the proxy variables. That was my own shell session inheriting them, not a leftover config file — the isolated re-test came back clean. Your currently-open terminal tabs have the same stale variables in memory, so **open a new terminal (or run `exec zsh`) before starting Claude**, otherwise the old proxy settings will still apply.

**Two things worth knowing:**

Since you declined a backup, the AgentRouter token is no longer stored anywhere on disk. If you ever want that setup back, the value was `sk-REDACTED` against base URL `https://agentrouter.org`. It's been sitting in plaintext in your shell config, so if you don't plan to reuse it, consider revoking it on AgentRouter's side.

Your gstack installation at `~/gstack` was not touched and its `bin` is still on your PATH, so the 270 agents, 56 skills, and hooks are reinstallable rather than lost — but note that reinstalling gstack's Claude integration is likely what re-adds the hooks to `settings.json`, so hold off if you want to stay stock.

Run `claude` in a new terminal and it will walk through first-time onboarding and browser login for `emutembei@appliedhealthanalytics.org`.
